native_result.query: What types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use is differentially associated with the three introduction pathways. Locally (plot scale), urban land use is most strongly linked to the Unintentional pathway: plots adjacent to urban areas have a higher proportional share of invasive species from accidental introductions (trade, contaminated seed lots, tourism) — adjusted OR ≈ 1.12 per +10% urban cover within 500 m (p ≈ 0.05; chi-square high- vs low-urban composition p = 0.004) — consisting of short, wide-niche weedy generalists. Gardening (ornamental) introductions are associated with less local urban exposure (composition OR ≈ 0.88, p ≈ 0.04; absolute IRR ≈ 0.93, p ≈ 0.03) and AgriForest introductions show no urban association (all p ≥ 0.07). Regionally, the Gardening pathway is the one that surged with urbanization: 41% of introductions pre-1985 vs 75% in 1985-2019 (p < 1e-46), the period when urban cover in plot buffers tripled. Thus urbanization-era introductions are dominated by Gardening/ornamental introductions regionally, while locally urban land use shifts invaded assemblages toward Unintentional, trade-mediated species; AgriForest introductions are not urban-linked.
native_result.WorkflowB: Inspected 4 files (632 plots; 81 species; 4x3 period x pathway table; 79-tip phylogeny). Binomial GLMs of per-plot pathway share (n_p of n_total) on urban_2009_500m with habitat, elevation, temperature, rainfall, distance to road/stream, cropland as covariates; robustness via no-habitat, urban-only, and all 9 urban buffer-year + change variables. Poisson GLMs (HC3) for absolute per-plot counts. Chi-square tests: high- vs low-urban composition, Urban vs other habitats, invasion probability, period x pathway. Species traits compared by pathway. All code in analysis.py; output in results.txt.
